fields.title: Worse, but working
fields.keyTakeaway: Degradation is designed in advance with a "what to show without this component" table, and an untested reduced mode fails precisely when needed.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The recommendation service is down. Show an empty screen, an error, or something else?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: The difference between a product that works worse during a partial outage and a product that stops working entirely is the difference in revenue during the incident. For Polka, 20 minutes of complete shutdown during the evening peak costs about 900 orders; the same outage with degradation would cost close to zero.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: [[graceful-degradation|Degradation]] is pre-designed reduced behavior. The key word is "pre-designed": nothing is designed during an incident.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: Four forms, from best to worst:
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Replacement.** Instead of personalized, popular items. The user does not notice. **Reduction.** A feature is unavailable, the rest works. Checkout without bonuses. **Deferred execution.** We accept it and will do it later. "Request accepted, we will confirm within an hour". **Honest refusal with explanation.** Worse than previous ones, better than a silent error.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: A PM's job is to answer in advance for every important scenario: **what do we show when the component is missing?** This is a one-page table, and it is made once.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: The second tool is a **[[kill-switch|kill switch]]**: the ability to turn off a feature in a minute without a release. Needed for anything heavy and non-essential. During an incident, this is the difference between "turned off in a minute" and "rolling out a hotfix for forty minutes".
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: The third is **[[traffic-prioritization|traffic prioritization]]**: when capacity is lacking, serve important traffic at the expense of secondary. Checkout is more important than viewing history. Configured in advance.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Degradation table compiled after the recommendations incident.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/1/1: Catalog by categories, search bar hidden
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Kill switches set up for recommendations, search, reviews, feed personalization. Tested once a quarter: turned on and off under test load.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: The first test found that the search switch did not work — when search was disabled, the app showed an empty screen instead of the catalog. Plan B, which was never used, failed precisely as `IN1-N5` warns.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Degradation has a limit: without the order database and without authorization, the product does not work at all. For such components, the answer is not degradation, but redundancy.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Degradation is designed in advance with a "what to show without this component" table, and an untested reduced mode fails precisely when needed.
